**Stonebeck: gains that outrun the ledger beneath them**

Rating: underweight

Calder & Root read the policy support as resolution.¹ We read it as anesthesia. The data panel shows a one_year_return of +15.0% and a ytd_return of +6.0%, with drawdown flat at +0.0% — a surface so calm it invites suspicion rather than comfort. Equities extend gains and issuance windows reopen, per the newsflow, yet none of this addresses the reported_vs_public_gap of -0.8%, which we take as the more honest number in the room. Marks lag reality; the ledger is always the last to know.

Consider the hy_spread_now_bps at 320bps against a policy_rate_now of 4.50% and cpi_now of 2.4%. Real financing costs remain restrictive even as risk appetite widens issuance windows. That combination — cheap-feeling equity markets sitting atop a credit spread that has not meaningfully compressed — is the kind of divergence that structurally cautious readers are trained to distrust. If one were to sketch the relevant chart, it would show the equity line climbing steadily through the quarter while the spread line runs nearly flat beside it, refusing to confirm the rally; two lines that should move together, drifting apart.²

The rival house's "stay the course" thesis presumes the gap between reported and public figures is noise. We treat it as signal — a lagging indicator of fragility building beneath a calm drawdown print. Reopened issuance windows can also be read as levered entities refinancing before conditions tighten again, not evidence of durable health.

The explicit risk to our own view: should spreads compress further alongside continued equity gains, our caution will look like excessive pessimism, and the reported-public gap may prove a data-lag artifact rather than a warning. We watch the spread-equity relationship closely before revising.

¹ Calder & Root, per the record above.
² Chart described, not attached, as is our habit.
